title: Trajectory Statistics & Uncertainty
intro: Poisson equations describe classwise means and fluctuations of one correlated trajectory, using compact atom labels without density-matrix histories.

semantics.label_indicator: f = 1 for the selected prepared-state label, otherwise 0. Edge labels represent U|xy⟩; Vertex labels represent |χ(x)⟩.
semantics.outcome_indicator: f = 1{Xₙ = v} uses the already recorded current outcome. For Edge (x,y), this outcome is x.
semantics.vertex_probability: f = Pr(Xₙ₊₁ = v | current atom) is evaluated analytically. It is a probability, not an additional sampled outcome.
semantics.coherence_real: A = |i⟩⟨j| + |j⟩⟨i| in the physical basis. f = Re tr(Aρₐₜₒₘ) preserves complex phases and introduces no extra measurement.
semantics.coherence_imag: A = −i|i⟩⟨j| + i|j⟩⟨i| in the physical basis. f = Re tr(Aρₐₜₒₘ) preserves complex phases and introduces no extra measurement.

stationaryStart: Stationary atom ensemble in a class
selectedClass: Class to inspect / prepare on next run
warmup: Warm-up does not guarantee stationarity. The standard error excludes finite transient bias. The trajectory seed is independent of the scattering seed.
stationaryHelp: This prepares a stationary atom ensemble explicitly. First run discovers the classes; select one and run again to prepare it. Absorption weights always describe the original experimental input.
invalid: Use integer N from 1 to 100000, warm-up from 0 to 10000, and seed from 0 to 4294967295. Coherence requires distinct basis indices and dimension at most 64.
singleClass: One recurrent class is reachable from the experimental input. Its additive-functional CLT applies; positive variance and numerical stability determine whether a Gaussian band is shown.
conditional: Several classes are reachable. The limiting time average is class dependent. Conditional Gaussian mixtures are not generally one global Gaussian, even when the class means agree.
periodic: Periodicity permits the finite-state Poisson equation and additive-functional CLT. It does not guarantee ordinary convergence of the state law from arbitrary input.
transient: Initial probability on transient labels: {{mass}}. Absorption weights include all of this mass.
correlationHelp: Time steps on one trajectory are correlated. The IID comparison assumes independence and is not the valid uncertainty estimate. Neither quantity describes deterministic channel-evolution error or independent-trajectory ensemble variance.
degenerate: σ² = 0: no nondegenerate Gaussian interval is drawn. Finite-length periodic errors and transient bias may still be nonzero.
unstable: The Poisson system is numerically sensitive. Inspect diagnostics; Gaussian intervals are suppressed.
classTable: Closed classes · aⱼ is absorption probability from the original experimental input
timing: Atoms begin at t = {{start}}. This run records N = {{n}} observations from t = {{first}} to {{last}}, with seed {{seed}}. Plot points may be thinned; every observation contributes to the mean.
preparedClass: This path was initialized in the stationary ensemble of class {{id}}.
differentClass: This path has not entered the selected class. Its reference line is for inspection; the band is hidden. Selecting a class does not resample the path.
supportWarning: The numerical support approximation removed transitions, or the path left an analyzed closed class. Sampling uses original dynamics; no empirical Gaussian band is shown for this approximation.
bandHelp: When shown, shading is μ ± zσ/√N at nominal {{confidence}}% confidence: an asymptotic pointwise envelope, not simultaneous coverage or an exact finite-sample guarantee. The final interval is centered at the empirical mean. Finite transient bias is excluded.
interval: Approximate final confidence interval for μ
values: Inspect atom values and empirical law
support: Support cutoff: {{cutoff}}; removed entries: {{count}}; maximum row L1 change: {{change}}.
numericalSupport: Classwise theory describes the numerical analysis matrix. Small residuals do not certify infinite-time accuracy after removing genuine tiny rates.
analyticSupport: Support is analytically declared. Original finite-time dynamics remain unchanged.
